subject: accordion
pitch:
Category: Object.
Subject: piano accordion.
Style: Italian mother-of-pearl.
reasoning:
I'm planning a TypeScript module for a static piano accordion model in an Italian mother-of-pearl style, sketching realistic proportions like a treble keyboard height around 0.4m and bellows width around 0.3m, built from b.part geometry pieces since it doesn't need joints.

I'm working out orientation: the keyboard facing +Z with the instrument's length running along the X axis, deciding how it should rest on the floor so the layout reads clearly to a viewer.

I'll settle on lying horizontally with the treble box at +X, bass at -X, and put the keyboard on the +Z face with keys as thin strips stacked along Y, each sticking outward along X toward the player.

Defining box height along Y at 0.42 and depth along Z at 0.22, resting on the floor like a display piece. The bass box at the -X end gets its own button grid on the same +Z-facing side.

Working through the treble box placement with its grille and register switches at the +X end, and pinning down the keyboard's exact x-range on the +Z face. I'm sketching coordinate ranges for both boxes and the bellows connecting them: treble around x 0.14-0.34, bass around x -0.34 to -0.14, bellows filling the 0.28 gap between.

For the bellows I'm planning an accordion fold of 14 pleats using alternating-scale boxes to fake the trapezoid pleat shape. For the color scheme, I'm going with an Italian-style look: pearlescent mother-of-pearl body tones with iridescent pink/aqua/lilac accents, dark bellows with white pearl papers, and gold corner protectors.

I'm designing a mosaic helper function that scatters small tinted boxes across the body's faces to simulate mother-of-pearl tiling, keeping the part count manageable by limiting mosaic density. I'm starting to lay out the main components, beginning with the treble box and keyboard placement.

Now I'm sorting out keyboard geometry: fitting white and black keys along the +Z face within the box's height constraint, adjusting key count and spacing so they fit properly, and figuring out how the keys should protrude outward from the recessed keybed.

Let me work out the actual dimensions for the keyboard panel — figuring out where the treble box sits in x, sizing the white keys around 0.11-0.13 long, and placing the shorter black keys offset toward one edge.

For the overall accordion layout, I'm setting up constants: body depth, height, the treble box spanning one side in x, the bass box mirrored on the other side, and the bellows connecting them in the middle with roughly 16 pleats.

Writing bellows pleat geometry...

I'll color the ridges and valleys with dark and red tones for contrast, then move on to detailing the treble box: a pearl-finished main body, with the keyboard on the front face, mosaic panels on the back, and a gold grille on the end.

For the grille, I'm designing a gold plate with vertical dark slots and a pearl-and-abalone diamond rosette at center, plus a small row of register switches that I'm now trying to place sensibly near the top end of the treble box.

For the treble strap, I'm adding a thin black leather strap on the back face with two gold buckles, built from simple boxes rather than a true curved loop.

For the bass box, I'm laying out the button grid on the end face—roughly 6 columns by 12 rows with small spaced buttons to match the bass side's scale.

Adding bin helper...

I'm also planning simplified details: a bass strap on the back face, gold L-bracket corner protectors along the box edges, and a pearl mosaic pattern on the treble and bass back faces, keeping color count under the 64 limit.

I'm extruding a diamond outline on the +X face with abalone edges, pearl fill, and a small gold center, then planning a gold "Maestro" name badge centered above the keys with margins calculated from the keyboard width.

For the badge, I'll place a small gold oval plane with text on the bass box's +Z face, skipping mosaic tiles that overlap that region, and I'm considering adding small gold feet at the base.

The boxes should rest directly at y=0 with bottoms touching the floor, maybe with pearl-trimmed gold corner protectors instead of separate feet. For keys, I'm detailing white keys in cream pearl and black keys in ebony, with slight gaps between them for realism.

I'm settling on all white keys as pearl-toned cream and black keys as a purple-black with a thin pearl inlay strip for accent, then calculating the x/y positions for each white key and figuring out which positions get black keys using the standard musical pattern (skipping between E-F and B-C).

Now I'm placing the gold/pearl cheek rails flanking the keyboard sides and adding gold trim strips along the treble edge near the keys. I'm also planning a bellows closure strap on the bass side with a gold buckle detail.

I'm positioning the bellows strap on top, stretching from the bass box over the bellows closure as a flat black band with a gold buckle ring, and considering a separate thumb strap on the treble back panel as another slim black band.

Skipping shoulder straps since they'd need to arch above the instrument with no support -- too complex to float properly. Instead I'm focusing on the treble grille: a gold plate with dark vertical slots spaced evenly across the face, framed with pearl inlay around the edges.

Simplifying further: the plate holds two slot blocks above and below a central diamond medallion rimmed in abalone, which reads cleaner than overlapping slots and diamond patterns. I'm placing register switches along a pearl strip on top of the treble box next.

Now I'm defining a general mosaic tiling helper that lays out tile boxes across a face given a center point, orientation axes, tile counts, and thickness, so I can reuse it across different panel surfaces.

Writing geometry bin class...

Still laying out buttons and hardware...

Adding dimensions and placement...

Still placing bellows ridges...

I'll skip the pearl inlay idea since the dark bellows and gold corners with red valleys already work well. Instead I'm adding thin gold frame plates along the sides at x=±0.15 connecting the boxes and bellows for structural cohesion.

I'm thinking about a label plate using an SVG texture with a gold ellipse background and cursive dark text reading something like "Bella Perla," applied to a small plane geometry above the keys. I'll skip the decorative pearl rosettes to keep things simpler, and now I'm positioning the keyboard keys relative to the box height.

Working out the keybed and key dimensions...

Defining mosaicZ tile placement...

I'll skip the top mosaic to limit effort, and set up helper functions for placing boxes and cylinders with proper rotation so cylinders can align along X or Z axes.

At the end I'll merge all geometries grouped by color into single meshes for efficiency, routing most shapes (boxes, base colors, keys, etc.) through these bins since they can hold roughly 25 distinct colors. For the diamond medallion I'll extrude a simple diamond-shaped outline.

Working out the exact x-offsets and thicknesses for the layered medallion pieces -- abalone ring, inner pearl ring, and gold center cylinder -- then placing the grille plate and mask so everything nests correctly before writing the badge geometry.

Now I'm figuring out where the grille slots sit relative to the diamond shape, making sure the dark slot boxes above and below don't intersect the diamond's vertical extent.

I'm placing the register switches along the top strip with alternating pearl-colored boxes, then positioning the bellows strap as a cover spanning from the bass side to the treble side.

Adding back strap boxes with gold rivet cylinders for both treble and bass sides, checking the mosaic tile overlap doesn't clash with strap placement, then moving to writing the actual generation code using the seeded rng function.
